llm.summary: The package largely matches its stated purpose (a multi-agent engineering suite with a persistent headless browser), but several installation and telemetry behaviors — plus a remote 'curl | bash' installer and a detected prompt-injection pattern — are disproportionate or need explicit scrutiny before installing.

dimensions.detail: The repository contents (browse daemon, 29 SKILL.md files, browser cookie import, agents, CLI, extension) align with the 'multi-agent engineering team' description. Items that need attention: telemetry/supabase functions, a Chrome extension, and scripts that modify ~/.agents/skills and OpenClaw config — these are plausible for this product but expand scope beyond a simple SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md's install instructions tell users to run a remote installer (curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh | bash) and to have the agent modify OpenClaw configuration and restart the gateway. The instructions imply creating files under the home directory, starting a persistent daemon, and requesting Keychain access to decrypt browser cookies — all of which are sensitive operations that go beyond passive skill invocation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Although the repo includes an install.sh, the SKILL.md recommends piping a raw GitHub URL into bash (curl | bash). Executing remote scripts directly is high-risk even when hosted on GitHub: the script runs arbitrary code on the user's machine. No alternative signed release channel or package registry is provided in the SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Metadata lists no required env vars, but documentation and test instructions reference ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other env-driven features for LLM-based tests. The project includes telemetry ingestion (supabase functions) and suggests collecting persistent eval artifacts in ~/.founderclaw-dev; cookie decryption requires Keychain/Keyring/DPAPI access. These are plausible for this tool but are sensitive (LLM keys, browser cookies, telemetry endpoints) and not declared in the minimal requires.env — an inconsistency worth reviewing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and is user-invocable (expected). It does, however, install long-lived components: a browse daemon that auto-starts on first use, writes state and logs under the user's home (~/.founderclaw / ~/.founderclaw-dev), and can modify OpenClaw skill symlinks and agent configuration. Those behaviors grant persistent presence and local privileges that are coherent for this product but should be accepted knowingly.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This project appears to be a full-featured multi-agent tooling suite and many of the sensitive behaviors (daemon, cookie decryption, config changes, telemetry) are coherent with that purpose — but you should not run the remote installer blindly. Before installing: 1) Inspect install.sh (and any scripts it downloads) locally (don't run curl | bash). 2) Confirm the GitHub repo/owner authenticity (the SKILL.md points to github.com/ashish797). 3) Review supabase/telemetry code and any remote endpoints the code contacts; decide whether you are comfortable with telemetry and what data is sent. 4) Verify you accept required operations: creating ~/.founderclaw, symlinking skills into ~/.agents/skills, and restarting/touching OpenClaw config. 5) Expect Keychain/Keyring/DPAPI prompts for cookie import — only approve if you trust the repo. 6) If possible, test inside a sandboxed environment or disposable account before installing on a primary machine. If you need higher assurance, request a reproducible signed release or vetted package rather than piping a raw GitHub script into bash.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern in SKILL.md. The project claims to inject ETHOS/preamble text into skills; however, any attempt to override or inject into system prompts is sensitive for agent platforms. This finding should be manually reviewed in the SKILL.md and preamble generation code to confirm it is only adding benign context, not attempting to alter platform-level system prompts.
